You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Compared with the source image, has the woman's jacket visibly moved toward closure while remaining not fully closed?
node.criteria: Pass only if comparable visual evidence shows the same jacket's front panels moved closer together from source to edited image, while a visible opening remains. Compare panel edges and opening width only in portions that are discernible in both images, accounting for pose and viewpoint changes. Fail only if comparable evidence shows no movement toward closure, no change, or a wider opening. Do not infer progress from turning, fabric flare, or motion alone. Unknown if the front opening or its change cannot be reliably compared.
node.binding: Compare the same jacket's front opening across the source and edited images. Seek comparable views of visible panel edges and opening width, accounting for pose and viewpoint changes; use only portions discernible in both images. Do not treat turning or flaring as evidence of progress. This check records partial progress only and does not satisfy the full-closure requirement.

node_traces.evidence: In the source, the woman faces mostly toward the camera and the jacket’s front opening is visible. In the edited image, she is turned sideways and the jacket fabric flares outward, so the same front-panel edges and opening width are not comparably discernible. The apparent change cannot reliably establish movement toward closure.

response.content: {"text":"The node is appropriately cautious about pose and fabric flare, but its binding makes comparable front-panel edges and opening width the only usable evidence. In these images the source shows a mostly frontal view with a visible dark center opening, while the edit turns the woman sideways and the jacket swings outward; that prevents a reliable width comparison, but does not by itself establish either progress or absence of progress. Keep this check limited to partial movement toward closure, and clarify how to assess any other directly visible, comparable evidence of the same jacket’s closure state without treating pose, flare, or motion as progress. If no such evidence is discernible, retain unknown rather than forcing a label. The trace is valid and queried with no dependency or transport failure, so this is an evidence/criterion robustness issue, not an execution failure. The aggregate reference label is not atomic ground truth and does not justify changing the criterion to force yes; investigate why the requested edit is unresolved under this view."}
